subject: Clarify output ownership / training carveouts for Order Form - HorizonCloud
messages:
From: HorizonCloud Legal <contracts@horizon.cloud>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Carl Singh <carl.singh@horizon.cloud>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Revised Order Form redlines — IP & training carveouts

Marcus —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are HorizonCloud's redlines to the Order Form and a short summary of concerns from legal/product. The core asks are:

- We need explicit assurance that outputs generated by Redwood using our customer data are owned by HorizonCloud (including derivatives).
- We require that Redwood not use HorizonCloud data to further train or improve models without affirmative opt-in (we asked for a no-training commitment).
- We want a feedback license limited to telemetry necessary for service health & abuse prevention, not a broad feedback/training license.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept language that: (a) assigns title to outputs to HorizonCloud for the term of the agreement, and (b) carves HorizonCloud data out of any training uses. If Redwood cannot accept programmatic title transfer, please propose alternative language that gives HorizonCloud the rights it needs for productization and downstream distribution.

We've also flagged a couple of places in the MSA cross-referenced by the Order Form — attached redline highlights. Happy to set a 30-min call if quicker.

Attachments: HorizonCloud_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf (redline), summary_for-legal.txt (notes)

Thanks,
Rachel (on behalf of HorizonCloud Legal)
Rachel Park | Senior Counsel, HorizonCloud
contracts@horizon.cloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: HorizonCloud Legal <contracts@horizon.cloud>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form redlines — IP & training carveouts

Rachel / Carl —

Thanks for sending the redlines and summary. I reviewed with Product and Legal briefly — looping in Karthik (product/legal interface) and Marissa (customer success/legal ops) to help get precise language in the Order Form and any MSA cross-refs.

Quick answers up front:
- We recognize the productization concern and want to get to a place that makes HorizonCloud comfortable while preserving standard service operations.
- We do have a standard customer opt-out for training; we can propose a clear carveout in the Order Form.
- Title transfer to outputs is not our default model; we typically grant customers broad, perpetual rights to use outputs. That said, we can propose alternative clauses that effectively provide HorizonCloud the rights it needs for productization (e.g., exclusive-ish usage rights for certain use-cases, or an assignment of title limited to customer-provided prompts/inputs + outputs for specified services).

Karthik / Marissa — can you review Horizon's redlines and propose concrete language we can share back this afternoon? If we can resolve most language in writing, we'll avoid a call.

Next steps: I'll await Karthik's proposed text and a short comparison doc. If Horizon wants a call, propose 2 slots tomorrow morning PT and we'll confirm.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, HorizonCloud Legal <contracts@horizon.cloud>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Revised Order Form redlines — IP & training carveouts

Rachel / Carl / Marcus —

Thanks — I reviewed the attached redline and sketched two short, alternate approaches. I pasted them below and attached a tracked Word with the exact edits. Please consider as proposals for the Order Form / MSA cross-ref.

Option A (Customer-first, conservative):
"Customer Output Ownership and Use: Redwood hereby grants Customer an exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide right, title, and license to all Outputs generated by Redwood's Services that are produced in response to Customer Data and Prompts; Customer may use, reproduce, distribute, and create Derivative Works of such Outputs for any purpose. Redwood shall not use Customer Data, Customer Outputs, or Customer Prompts to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any production models used to serve other customers without Customer's prior written consent."

Option B (Operationally pragmatic):
"Customer Rights to Outputs: Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs generated from Customer Data for Customer's internal and external productization. Redwood retains the right to use de-identified telemetry for model health and safety. Redwood agrees not to use Customer Data, Customer Outputs, or identifiable Customer Prompts to train models for third-party use without Customer opt-in. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain non-identifying aggregate metrics and logs for service improvement and security."

Notes:
- Option A approximates assignment but uses a grant phrasing to avoid downstream support/escrow complexity. It is more likely to satisfy Horizon's legal stance on "ownership."
- Option B is closer to our baseline and preserves the ability to operate and improve the service while promising a training opt-out for Horizon.

If Horizon insists on title assignment language, we'll need the scope limited (e.g., specific product lines or services) and a finite transition window to ensure we don't break model provenance obligations.

Attachment: Redwood_proposed-ip-language.docx (tracked changes)

Marcus / Marissa: I recommend sending Option B with highlighted concessions to Horizon first, and offering Option A as a fallback during legal bilateral negotiation.

-karthik
Principal Product Counsel

From: HorizonCloud Legal <contracts@horizon.cloud>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Carl Singh <carl.singh@horizon.cloud>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 08:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form redlines — IP & training carveouts

Karthik / Marcus —

Thanks for the clear alternatives. We reviewed Option B with Product and Legal. Option B's operational language is much closer to what we can accept, provided a few clarifications:

1) We need explicit language that "non-identifying aggregate metrics" cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct customer outputs or prompts; suggest adding "where feasible" limits and an audit right for HorizonCloud once annually.
2) We require the training opt-out to be effective immediately upon execution of the Order Form (not after a notice period).
3) For any future feature that would use Customer Data for training at a later date, Redwood must notify HorizonCloud and obtain written consent (email is OK).

If Redwood can accept those clarifications in a short amendment to Option B, we can proceed to finalize. Otherwise we'll ask our procurement to escalate to a negotiation call.

Also — can Redwood confirm whether the telemetry logs we discuss include request/response payloads stored for >30 days? We are okay with short retention for operational debugging but not indefinite retention of raw outputs.

Would you be able to incorporate the clarifications and return a final marked Order Form?

Regards,
Rachel Park | Senior Counsel, HorizonCloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: HorizonCloud Legal <contracts@horizon.cloud>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Carl Singh <carl.singh@horizon.cloud>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form redlines — IP & training carveouts

Rachel / Carl —

Appreciate the quick review and clear asks. We're comfortable with Option B plus the three clarifications you listed; Karthik has updated the text to incorporate: (i) an explicit non-reconstruction sentence, (ii) training opt-out effective on signature, and (iii) requirement for written consent before any future training uses. We also clarified telemetry retention: raw request/response payloads retained a max of 30 days by default, with customer-controlled retention settings available for private deployments.

I've attached the marked Order Form with the incorporated clarifications and a short summary of changes. If that looks good to you, please sign the Order Form and we'll push the MSA crossrefs through legal. If you'd like a quick 20-min sync, Marcus (me) can do tomorrow 9:00–9:30 PT.

Attachments: HorizonCloud_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf (updated), Redwood_proposed-ip-language.docx (final tracked)

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
